notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plate has the blue EU strip plus the national coat of arms on a red circle, visible even through the blur.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Most common bollard is white with a black top, a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black on white or red on yellow. Albania uses white on black.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails are often rusty, and both A-type and B-type are common, unlike in the rest of the Balkans.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Simple round concrete or wooden poles.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: All Generation 4 coverage is smallcam: mounted low, with a big round blur and a small protrusion at the front.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 coverage sometimes has stitching rifts, also common in Albania. Coastal rounds almost never have them and use a short antenna.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Small and mountainous: lush green inland peaks, pale exposed rock on coastal ones; many roads have only 1 or 2 lanes.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Green farming valleys with deforested hills are most often seen in the north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A busy tourist bay with people in swimwear and a steep rocky ridge behind.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dry, treeless mountains around the capital and south of it, with vineyards.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Pine forests in the north and just north of Nikšić, most commonly in the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Grassy, treeless high-altitude mountains mark the national park around Žabljak, which also has unique architecture.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The capital stands out for modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The lake bridge has a railway and stone bollards next to the road.
